The intelligent treadmill comprises a treadmill body and an intelligent speed control system. The treadmill body includes a running deck and a motor for driving the running belt. To improve the user’s exercise experience and enhance operational safety, the running deck is divided into three functional areas: an acceleration section, a holding section, and a deceleration section.

The intelligent speed control system is configured to monitor the user’s position on the treadmill in real time. In particular, the system uses infrared array sensors to detect the position of the user’s center of gravity while the user is walking or running on the deck. The sensor data is transmitted to a processor module, which analyzes the detected center of gravity and determines whether it is located in the holding section, the acceleration section, or the deceleration section.

When the processor module determines that the user’s center of gravity is in the acceleration section, the treadmill may increase the running speed in a controlled manner. When the center of gravity is in the holding section, the treadmill maintains a stable speed suitable for the user’s current pace. When the center of gravity moves into the deceleration section, the treadmill may reduce the running speed to help prevent the user from drifting too far backward on the deck.

Through this intelligent speed adjustment mechanism, the treadmill can automatically adapt to the user’s movement without requiring frequent manual speed changes. As a result, the treadmill provides a safer, more stable, and more convenient exercise experience, reducing the risk of missteps while allowing the user to maintain a natural walking or running rhythm.

An intelligent treadmill is designed to automatically regulate its running-belt speed by sensing the user’s position on the deck and responding in real time. The system includes an infrared-array sensing device for detecting the user’s center of gravity, a processor for analyzing the sensing data, a motor driver for controlling the treadmill motor, and a running deck divided into configurable functional sections. These sections may include a holding section, an acceleration section, and a deceleration section, each corresponding to a different control response.

During use, the infrared-array sensing device continuously monitors the position of the user on the treadmill and determines where the user’s center of gravity is located. The processor receives this information and compares the detected center-of-gravity position with the predefined deck sections. If the user remains in the holding section, the treadmill maintains the current belt speed. If the user moves toward the acceleration section, the processor determines that the user intends or is able to run faster and sends a control signal to the motor driver to increase the belt speed. If the user moves toward the deceleration section, the processor determines that the user is falling behind or needs to slow down and instructs the motor driver to reduce the belt speed.

The positions and sizes of the holding, acceleration, and deceleration sections may be configured according to the user’s running habits, exercise mode, body characteristics, or training requirements. This allows the treadmill to provide a more personalized and adaptive exercise experience. Instead of requiring the user to manually press speed buttons or rely on preset programs, the treadmill can adjust automatically based on the user’s actual movement and center-of-gravity changes.

By using infrared-array center-of-gravity sensing and intelligent speed control, the treadmill can respond more quickly and accurately to changes in the user’s running state. This improves control efficiency, reduces the delay associated with manual adjustment, and helps keep the user in a stable and comfortable running position. As a result, the system enhances exercise safety, reduces the risk of stumbling or drifting too far forward or backward on the belt, and provides a smarter, more stable treadmill workout experience.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, but it is also one of the most important. It is called the definite article, and it helps us talk about specific people, places, things, or ideas. For example, when we say “a book,” we may mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

Although “the” is simple, it gives sentences clarity and direction. It can point to something already mentioned, something unique, or something well known. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our sky, and we say “the teacher” when everyone knows which teacher we mean.

The word “the” may not seem exciting, but without it, English would sound unclear and incomplete. It is a small word with a big role, helping people communicate more precisely every day.

counterfactuals.output: An intelligent treadmill system is disclosed for automatically adjusting belt speed in response to a runner’s position as determined from the runner’s center of gravity. The system includes a treadmill frame, an endless running belt driven by a motor, a motor controller, one or more infrared array sensors arranged to detect thermal image data of a runner on the running belt, a processor communicatively coupled to the infrared array sensors and the motor controller, and a memory storing control instructions. The processor receives infrared array data, identifies a human body region, calculates a center-of-gravity position of the runner relative to a predefined reference zone of the running surface, and generates a speed control command according to displacement of the center-of-gravity position. When the center of gravity moves forward of the reference zone, the processor increases belt speed; when the center of gravity moves rearward of the reference zone, the processor decreases belt speed; and when the center of gravity remains within the reference zone, the processor maintains the current speed. The control method includes acquiring infrared array signals, filtering noise, determining a runner position map, estimating the center of gravity, comparing the estimated center of gravity with one or more threshold regions, calculating a speed adjustment value, and transmitting the adjustment value to the motor controller to regulate the running belt. The system thereby provides hands-free, adaptive treadmill speed control while reducing reliance on wearable devices or manual input.

A smart treadmill includes a running deck divided along a longitudinal direction into an acceleration zone, a holding zone, and a deceleration zone. A belt is driven by a motor under control of a motor driver. A gravity-center sensing device is arranged to detect a user’s center-of-gravity position or pressure distribution on the deck and to generate corresponding sensing signals. A processor receives the sensing signals, determines whether the user is located in the acceleration zone, holding zone, or deceleration zone, and outputs a speed-control command to the motor driver.

When the detected center of gravity moves toward the front acceleration zone, the processor commands the motor driver to increase belt speed. When the center of gravity remains within the intermediate holding zone, the processor maintains the current belt speed. When the center of gravity shifts toward the rear deceleration zone, the processor commands the motor driver to reduce belt speed. In this manner, the treadmill automatically adapts belt speed to the user’s natural running position without requiring manual speed adjustment.

The treadmill may further include a host computer communicatively connected to the processor. The host computer stores exercise parameters, displays running information, receives user settings, and may execute control programs for training modes, safety limits, calibration, or data analysis. The gravity-center sensing device may include pressure sensors, load cells, force plates, optical sensors, or other position-detection elements distributed beneath or around the running deck.

The invention provides an intelligent speed-control treadmill capable of detecting a user’s forward or rearward displacement on the running surface and automatically accelerating, holding, or decelerating the belt accordingly, thereby improving exercise convenience, safety, and responsiveness.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical summary of a treadmill speed control system where the user sets holding-section limits and a speed adjustment ratio, and the treadmill detects body center-of-gravity position to control acceleration or deceleration.
counterfactuals.output:
A treadmill speed control system allows a user to define a “holding section” on the running belt and set a speed adjustment ratio used for automatic speed correction. The holding section represents a target zone in which the runner’s body center of gravity should remain during normal exercise.

The system includes a body-position detection unit that estimates the runner’s center-of-gravity position relative to the treadmill belt, typically along the longitudinal direction of movement. This position may be detected using sensors such as pressure sensors, optical sensors, cameras, load cells, or other motion/position detection devices.

During operation, the controller compares the detected center-of-gravity position with the user-defined holding-section limits:

- If the runner’s center of gravity remains within the holding section, the treadmill maintains the current belt speed.
- If the center of gravity moves forward beyond the front limit of the holding section, the controller determines that the runner is moving faster than the belt and increases belt speed.
- If the center of gravity moves rearward beyond the rear limit of the holding section, the controller determines that the runner is falling behind and decreases belt speed.

The amount of acceleration or deceleration is determined according to the preset speed adjustment ratio. This ratio defines how strongly the treadmill speed is changed in response to the detected displacement of the user’s center of gravity outside the holding section. A larger ratio produces faster speed correction, while a smaller ratio provides smoother, more gradual adjustment.

The control process can be summarized as follows:

1. Receive user settings for the holding-section front and rear limits.
2. Receive a user setting for the speed adjustment ratio.
3. Detect the runner’s body center-of-gravity position.
4. Compare the detected position with the holding-section limits.
5. Maintain speed if the center of gravity is inside the holding section.
6. Increase speed if the center of gravity is ahead of the front limit.
7. Decrease speed if the center of gravity is behind the rear limit.
8. Apply the speed change according to the selected adjustment ratio.

This approach enables adaptive treadmill speed regulation without requiring the user to manually press speed controls during exercise. By keeping the runner’s center of gravity within a predefined safe operating zone, the system improves running comfort, responsiveness, and safety while allowing a more natural exercise experience.

An intelligent treadmill and control method are provided. The treadmill includes a treadmill body, a running belt driven by a motor, and a deck structure divided into a plurality of deck sections corresponding to different running or walking regions. The motor driver adjusts the operating speed of the motor, including acceleration, deceleration, or stopping of the running belt, in response to the control instructions. ## Invention Disclosure: Intelligent Center-of-Gravity Controlled Treadmill

### Title  
**Intelligent Treadmill with Automatic Speed Control Based on User Center of Gravity**

### Technical Field  
This invention relates to exercise equipment, and more particularly to a motorized treadmill that automatically adjusts belt speed by sensing a user’s center of gravity or position on the running surface.

### Background  
Conventional treadmills require users to manually adjust speed or use preset programs. This can be inconvenient and may interrupt natural walking or running rhythm. Existing automatic systems may rely on limited position sensing and may not provide intuitive speed control based on the user’s movement intent.

### Summary of the Invention  
The disclosed treadmill includes sensors configured to detect the user’s center of gravity relative to the treadmill deck. The deck is divided into at least three functional regions: an acceleration section, a holding or constant-speed section, and a deceleration section. A controller determines the user’s center-of-gravity location and automatically controls the treadmill motor speed based on the detected section.

When the user’s center of gravity is detected in the acceleration section, the controller increases belt speed. When the center of gravity is detected in the holding section, the controller maintains the current belt speed. When the center of gravity is detected in the deceleration section, the controller decreases belt speed.

### Key Components  
- A treadmill frame and moving belt driven by a motor  
- One or more sensors for detecting user center of gravity or load distribution  
- A controller configured to process sensor signals  
- A motor drive circuit responsive to controller commands  
- Defined deck regions corresponding to acceleration, holding, and deceleration control zones  

### Example Operation  
Load sensors, pressure sensors, force plates, optical sensors, or inertial sensing may determine the user’s center of gravity along the longitudinal direction of the treadmill. If the user moves forward on the deck, the system interprets this as a desire to accelerate and increases motor speed. If the user remains near the central holding zone, the system maintains speed. If the user drifts rearward, the system reduces speed to help return the user to the holding zone.

### Novel Features  
- Automatic treadmill speed adjustment based on detected center of gravity  
- Division of the treadmill surface into acceleration, holding, and deceleration sections  
- Real-time motor control responsive to natural user positioning  
- Hands-free speed control without manual input  
- Potential improvement in safety, comfort, and exercise fluidity  

### Potential Claims  
1. A treadmill comprising a belt, motor, center-of-gravity sensing system, and controller configured to adjust motor speed according to whether the detected center of gravity lies in an acceleration, holding, or deceleration section.  
2. The treadmill of claim 1, wherein the sensing system includes pressure, load, optical, or force sensors.  
3. The treadmill of claim 1, wherein motor speed is increased, maintained, or decreased based on the respective detected section.  
4. The treadmill of claim 1, wherein the controller continuously updates speed to maintain the user’s center of gravity within the holding section.
